iterations.note: First review of all stories (1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 7, 8, 4) against each other, DECISIONS.md and the Assignment 1 designs

Second review before building story 1: SPEC.md unchanged since iteration 1, so all open findings stay open; 9 new findings, mostly from rules written in iteration 1 (#29, #28) and checks across stories
Re-check after the iteration 2 decisions: only story 1 changed (#19, #29, #30 approved); the new text resolves them and adds no new findings

findings.title: Condition is scored per version, but condition belongs to each copy (listing)

evidence.where: Story 3 · How the pick is made
evidence.quote: Each version has a score from 1 to 5 for each criterion: sound, price, original, condition (illustrative data)
Listing: claimed version, actual version, price, condition, seller, city, photos

proposal.section: Story 3 · How the pick is made
proposal.current: Each version has a score from 1 to 5 for each criterion: sound, price, original, condition (illustrative data)
proposal.proposed: Sound and original scores (1–5) are stored per version (illustrative data). The condition score is calculated: the best condition among the version's listings on sale (M = 5, NM = 4, VG+ = 3, VG = 2, G = 1).

resolution.decision: Approved. Condition score = best condition among the version's active listings. Grade values may change with #8.

findings.title: Price score is stored per version, while real prices live in the listings and change

evidence.where: Story 3 · How the pick is made
evidence.quote: Each version has a score from 1 to 5 for each criterion: sound, price, original, condition
number of listings, lowest price

proposal.section: Story 3 · How the pick is made
proposal.proposed: The price score is calculated from each version's lowest active price: 5 × (cheapest lowest price ÷ this version's lowest price), rounded, minimum 1.

resolution.decision: Approved with a revised formula: 5 × (cheapest ÷ this lowest price), rounded, min 1. The first proposal (cheapest = 5, dearest = 1) was dropped because it changed the example result.

findings.title: Reasons are fixed per version, but Assignment 1 asks for reasons tied to the buyer's priorities

evidence.quote: Reason text: fixed sentences per version
One version, with reasons tied to my priorities
e.g. "Costs €32, vs €185 for a first pressing"

proposal.section: Story 3 · Data used / What the screen shows
proposal.current: Reason text: fixed sentences per version
proposal.proposed: Reason text: fixed sentences per version and per criterion (sound, price, original, condition). The screen shows the sentences for the buyer's chosen priorities, in rank order (max 3). Prices inside sentences come from the data, not from the text.

resolution.decision: Approved. One sentence per version and criterion, shown for the chosen priorities in rank order (max 3); prices from the data.

findings.title: Which listings count for a version is not defined (counts, lowest price, "No listings", "has listings")

evidence.quote: label "No listings" when the album has no active listings

evidence.where: Story 3 · How the pick is made
evidence.quote: Only versions with at least one active listing can be recommended
Red listing → appears here as a warning and also under the correct version

proposal.section: New section before Story 1 · Shared rules
proposal.proposed: Active listing: a listing on sale (not sold, not removed) that is green or yellow. Counts, lowest price, "No listings" and "has listings" use active listings only. A red listing counts for its actual version, not for the version the seller claimed.

resolution.decision: Approved. New 'Shared rules' section in SPEC.md defines active listings; all counts and prices use them; red listings count for their actual version.

findings.title: Album with no listings leads the buyer through the priorities screen to a dead end

evidence.quote: Album with no listings → shown, not hidden
Tapping an album opens the priorities screen (story 2)
No version of the album has listings → no recommendation; message: "Nobody is selling this album right now"

proposal.current: Tapping an album opens the priorities screen (story 2)
proposal.proposed: Tapping an album with active listings opens the priorities screen (story 2). Tapping an album with no listings shows "Nobody is selling this album right now" directly, without the priorities screen.

findings.question: Should an album with no listings skip the priorities screen and show the message straight away?

resolution.decision: Approved. Album with no listings shows the message directly; story 3 edge case updated.

findings.title: Traffic light of a red listing once it appears under its correct version is undefined

evidence.quote: appears here as a warning and also under the correct version, where it is checked again
Check result: listing, item (cover/label, country/year, matrix), result

proposal.proposed: where it is shown yellow ("Moved here · check pending"), because its checklist was made against the claimed version, not this one.

findings.question: Under its correct version, should a moved listing show yellow until it is checked again?

resolution.decision: Approved. Under its correct version a moved listing is yellow ('Moved here · check pending').

findings.title: "Suggestions close to the typed text" cannot be tested: no rule for how close or how many

evidence.quote: A search with no matches shows suggestions close to the typed text ("Did you mean Ziggy Stardust?")

proposal.current: A search with no matches shows suggestions close to the typed text
proposal.proposed: A search with no matches shows up to 3 album titles that differ from the typed text by at most 2 letters (e.g. "zigy" → "Did you mean Ziggy Stardust?"). With no such album, it shows "No albums found".

resolution.decision: Approved. Up to 3 album titles at most 2 letters away; otherwise 'No albums found'.

findings.title: Search results in the design show "from €24 · 3 verified copies"; the story moved price to the detail page without recording why

evidence.quote: Ziggy Stardust · David Bowie, 1972 · from €24 · 3 verified copies · 477 versions
Search result: cover, album title, artist, release year, number of versions

proposal.proposed:
### Search results show no price or listing count (story 1 · finding #19)
- Why: "from €24" is the cheapest copy of any pressing, often not the one Spindle recommends; it anchors the buyer on a price the recommendation then contradicts. Whether an album can be bought is already shown by the "No listings" label.

findings.question: Keep the results without price and copies (then record why), or follow the design?

resolution.decision: Keep the SPEC: no price or listing count in search results; reason recorded in DECISIONS.md (the cheapest copy of any pressing anchors the buyer on the wrong price).

Which rule decides the "ideal" version: (a) only the stored scores (sound, original), and the note appears only when the buyer's 1st priority is sound or original; (b) the full total, with price and condition counted as 0; or (c) drop the note from the MVP?

findings.title: "At most 2 letters different" from what? Against the full title, the story's own example fails

evidence.quote: A search with no matches shows up to 3 album titles that differ from the typed text by at most 2 letters (e.g. "zigy" → "Did you mean *Ziggy Stardust*?")
"ziggy" returns *The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust…*

proposal.section: Story 1 · Acceptance criteria and Edge cases
proposal.current: A search with no matches shows up to 3 album titles that differ from the typed text by at most 2 letters (e.g. "zigy" → "Did you mean *Ziggy Stardust*?")
proposal.proposed: A search with no matches shows up to 3 albums with a word in the title or artist name close to the typed text: at most 1 letter different when 4–5 letters are typed, at most 2 when 6 or more are typed; each suggestion shows the full album title. With 3 letters typed and no matches, only "No albums found".

findings.question: Compare the typed text with each word of the title and artist (proposal), or with the whole title?

resolution.decision: Approved with a revised rule: compare the typed text with each word of the title and artist; 1 letter for 4–5 letters typed, 2 for 6+; no suggestions with 3 letters; suggestions show the full title.

findings.title: The search does not say whether it ignores upper/lower case and accents

evidence.quote: The search matches the **album title** and the **artist name**; results are always **albums**
"ziggy" returns *The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust…*

proposal.proposed: - Matching ignores upper and lower case and accents (e.g. "bjork" finds "Björk")

resolution.decision: Approved. Matching ignores upper and lower case and accents.

Search results without price and copies (record why), or follow the design?
